chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn A'ith from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtār who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man enter into ihram wearing a black garment?' He said: 'He does not enter into ihram in a black garment, nor is the deceased shrouded in it.'

key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into the state of ritual consecration (ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing black clothes during Hajj ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the prohibition of black garments for ihram is linked to their historical association with the Umayyad caliphs, distinguishing them from the Prophetic tradition of white. This ruling extends to the funeral shroud (kafan), establishing black as an impure or distinct color for the deceased, reflecting the Shia emphasis on emulating the Ahl al-Bayt's practices in ritual purity and dress.
